Introduction.theory: Binary tree nodes have value, left and right references; either child may be null. Root has no parent. Height here counts nodes on a longest downward path; empty height is zero. Depth counts edges from root. A tree has no cycles or shared child nodes. Traversals visit every node in O(n): preorder root-left-right, inorder left-root-right, postorder left-right-root, level order breadth-first. General binary trees have no sorted-key property. Recursive traversals use O(h) call stack, possibly O(n) for a chain.

Inorder Traversal.approach: Recurse on both children, visiting the root in the position defined by this traversal. Each subtree is visited exactly once.
Inorder Traversal.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) stack plus O(n) output.
Inorder Traversal.trace: For root 4 with children 2,6, the position of 4 relative to both child traversals distinguishes the three orders.
Inorder Traversal.pitfalls: Null produces an empty output; values need not be unique. A deep chain can exhaust the call stack.
Inorder Traversal.alternatives: Iterative stacks avoid recursive frames but still require O(h) working storage.

Preorder Traversal.approach: Recurse on both children, visiting the root in the position defined by this traversal. Each subtree is visited exactly once.
Preorder Traversal.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) stack plus O(n) output.
Preorder Traversal.trace: For root 4 with children 2,6, the position of 4 relative to both child traversals distinguishes the three orders.
Preorder Traversal.pitfalls: Null produces an empty output; values need not be unique. A deep chain can exhaust the call stack.
Preorder Traversal.alternatives: Iterative stacks avoid recursive frames but still require O(h) working storage.

Postorder Traversal.approach: Recurse on both children, visiting the root in the position defined by this traversal. Each subtree is visited exactly once.
Postorder Traversal.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) stack plus O(n) output.
Postorder Traversal.trace: For root 4 with children 2,6, the position of 4 relative to both child traversals distinguishes the three orders.
Postorder Traversal.pitfalls: Null produces an empty output; values need not be unique. A deep chain can exhaust the call stack.
Postorder Traversal.alternatives: Iterative stacks avoid recursive frames but still require O(h) working storage.

Level Order Traversal.problem: Return values grouped by depth, left-to-right.
Level Order Traversal.approach: Capture queue size before processing a level. Children enter the queue for the next level; the captured bound prevents mixing levels.
Level Order Traversal.pitfalls: ArrayDeque forbids null; enqueue only existing children.

Pre, Post, Inorder in one traversal.problem: Return [preorder,inorder,postorder] from a single recursive walk.
Pre, Post, Inorder in one traversal.approach: Record a root at entry, between children, and at exit respectively. These are the three natural phases of a depth-first call.
Pre, Post, Inorder in one traversal.complexity: O(n) time and output, O(h) stack.
Pre, Post, Inorder in one traversal.trace: At root 4: pre records 4 before left, in after left, post after right.
Pre, Post, Inorder in one traversal.pitfalls: The returned order of the three lists is explicit and may differ from another platform's API.

Maximum Depth in BT.problem: Longest root-to-leaf path in NODES; empty depth is zero.
Maximum Depth in BT.approach: A subtree height is one plus the larger child height.
Maximum Depth in BT.trace: Sample tree has three levels; its unequal mirrored values and root 4 != 2+6 make symmetry/children-sum checks false.
Maximum Depth in BT.pitfalls: Be explicit about checking versus modifying the children-sum property. An empty tree passes boolean structural checks.

Check if two trees are identical or not.approach: Both null matches; one null fails; otherwise roots and both corresponding subtrees must match.
Check if two trees are identical or not.trace: Sample tree has three levels; its unequal mirrored values and root 4 != 2+6 make symmetry/children-sum checks false.
Check if two trees are identical or not.pitfalls: Be explicit about checking versus modifying the children-sum property. An empty tree passes boolean structural checks.

Check for balanced binary tree.problem: Every node's two subtree heights must differ by at most one.
Check for balanced binary tree.approach: Return height when balanced, or -1 sentinel for imbalance. Postorder computes each child height once and propagates failure.
Check for balanced binary tree.trace: Sample child heights are equal at every internal node.
Check for balanced binary tree.pitfalls: Checking only root balance is insufficient.
Check for balanced binary tree.alternatives: Recomputing subtree height at each node is O(n²) worst time.

Diameter of Binary Tree.problem: Return the longest path length in EDGES between any two nodes.
Diameter of Binary Tree.approach: A longest path has a highest node where its left and right downward paths meet. For each root, child heights sum to its through-root edge count; maximize globally.
Diameter of Binary Tree.pitfalls: A diameter need not pass through the global root. Singleton diameter is zero.

Maximum path sum.problem: Return maximum sum of a NONEMPTY simple path in a nonempty binary tree.
Maximum path sum.approach: Negative child gains can be omitted. Update the complete path using both sides, but return only one side because a parent cannot extend a fork.
Maximum path sum.pitfalls: Initialize global best to -infinity for all-negative trees, and use long sums.

Check for symmetrical BTs.problem: Check mirror symmetry of structure AND values about the root.
Check for symmetrical BTs.approach: Compare the left child of one side with the right child of the other.
Check for symmetrical BTs.trace: Sample tree has three levels; its unequal mirrored values and root 4 != 2+6 make symmetry/children-sum checks false.
Check for symmetrical BTs.pitfalls: Be explicit about checking versus modifying the children-sum property. An empty tree passes boolean structural checks.

Children Sum Property in Binary Tree.problem: Check whether each nonleaf value equals its children's values, with missing child zero.
Children Sum Property in Binary Tree.approach: Test local equality and recursively require it at all descendants. This lesson checks the property; it does not increase values to enforce it.
Children Sum Property in Binary Tree.trace: Sample tree has three levels; its unequal mirrored values and root 4 != 2+6 make symmetry/children-sum checks false.
Children Sum Property in Binary Tree.pitfalls: Be explicit about checking versus modifying the children-sum property. An empty tree passes boolean structural checks.

Zig Zag or Spiral Traversal.problem: Return level order alternating left-to-right then right-to-left.
Zig Zag or Spiral Traversal.approach: Compute level groups with BFS, then reverse odd-indexed levels. Reversal changes ordering only, preserving depth membership.
Zig Zag or Spiral Traversal.trace: Level 0 [4], reverse level 1 to [6,2], level 2 stays [1,3,5,7].
Zig Zag or Spiral Traversal.pitfalls: Do not reverse child enqueue order without a carefully matched traversal invariant.

Boundary Traversal.problem: Anticlockwise boundary: root, left boundary excluding leaves, leaves left-to-right, reversed right boundary excluding leaves.
Boundary Traversal.approach: Collect each role separately. Excluding leaves from boundaries prevents duplication; root is omitted initially if it is itself a leaf.
Boundary Traversal.trace: Sample: root 4; left boundary 2; leaves 1,3,5,7; reversed right boundary 6.
Boundary Traversal.pitfalls: For missing left/right children use the available child while following a boundary.

Vertical Order Traversal.problem: Group by horizontal column; within a column sort by depth, then value for same depth.
Vertical Order Traversal.approach: Assign coordinates root(0,0), left(-1,+1), right(+1,+1). Sort the coordinate records by the exact tie rules and group equal columns.
Vertical Order Traversal.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
Vertical Order Traversal.trace: Column zero contains 4 at depth 0 and values 3,5 at depth 2.
Vertical Order Traversal.pitfalls: BFS order alone is insufficient when same-coordinate ties require numeric order.

Top View of BT.problem: Return one visible value per column from left to right. Bottom-view equal-depth ties choose the later BFS node.
Top View of BT.approach: BFS visits shallow nodes first. Retain the first per column for the shallowest. TreeMap emits columns in ascending order.
Top View of BT.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
Top View of BT.trace: Column zero has 4 first, then 3 and 5; top retains 4, bottom retains 5.
Top View of BT.pitfalls: Tie rules vary by platform; bottom here uses later left-to-right BFS order.

Bottom view of BT.problem: Return one visible value per column from left to right. Bottom-view equal-depth ties choose the later BFS node.
Bottom view of BT.approach: BFS visits shallow nodes first. Overwrite per column to retain the latest/deepest. TreeMap emits columns in ascending order.
Bottom view of BT.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
Bottom view of BT.trace: Column zero has 4 first, then 3 and 5; top retains 4, bottom retains 5.
Bottom view of BT.pitfalls: Tie rules vary by platform; bottom here uses later left-to-right BFS order.

Right/Left View of BT.problem: Return [rightView,leftView], one visible value per depth.
Right/Left View of BT.approach: The last and first values respectively in each left-to-right BFS level define the views.
Right/Left View of BT.pitfalls: Horizontal columns used for top/bottom views do not define side views.

Print root to leaf path in BT.problem: Return all full root-to-leaf paths, left-first.
Print root to leaf path in BT.approach: DFS appends current value; copy at a leaf, recurse otherwise, then remove current before returning.
Print root to leaf path in BT.complexity: O(n+total emitted path lengths) time; O(h) working state plus output.
Print root to leaf path in BT.trace: Path 4,2 branches into leaves 1 and 3; after backtracking 4,6 branches into 5 and 7.
Print root to leaf path in BT.pitfalls: A leaf has neither child. Copy paths rather than storing the shared mutable builder.

LCA in BT.problem: Find lowest common ancestor by NODE identity; both query nodes must exist in the tree.
LCA in BT.approach: A subtree returns a found query or its LCA. If both children return nonnull, current root is the first meeting point; otherwise propagate the single found side.
LCA in BT.trace: Queries nodes 1 and 3 lie in opposite children of node 2, so LCA is 2.
LCA in BT.pitfalls: Equal values do not imply the same node. If either node may be absent, validate membership first; this kernel assumes presence.

Maximum Width of BT.problem: Width includes missing positions between leftmost/rightmost existing nodes at a level; return exact BigInteger.
Maximum Width of BT.approach: Assign conceptual complete-tree indices. Normalize each level by its first index, preserving differences. Width is last normalized index+1. BigInteger avoids exponential-gap overflow.
Maximum Width of BT.complexity: O(n) index operations plus index bit costs; O(maxWidthInNodes) queue storage.
Maximum Width of BT.trace: Full sample last level has indices 0,1,2,3, width four.
Maximum Width of BT.pitfalls: Count of actual level nodes differs from indexed width on sparse trees. Even normalization alone cannot prevent long overflow for very wide sparse gaps.

Print all nodes at a distance of K in BT.problem: Return values exactly k edges from a given target node; target must be in the tree.
Print all nodes at a distance of K in BT.approach: Map parent links, then BFS from target using left,right,parent as graph neighbors. Identity-based seen prevents walking back and forth; layer k is distance k.
Print all nodes at a distance of K in BT.complexity: O(n) time/space (this teaching helper computes all layers).
Print all nodes at a distance of K in BT.pitfalls: An optimized distance-k BFS can stop after k layers. Equal values remain separate node identities.

Minimum time taken to burn the BT from a.problem: Fire starts at target at time zero and spreads one edge per unit time; return time until all tree nodes burn.
Minimum time taken to burn the BT from a.approach: Reuse undirected BFS from the target. The last layer number is the farthest distance, which determines completion time.
Minimum time taken to burn the BT from a.trace: From leaf 1, leaf 7 is reached via 1,2,4,6,7 at time four.
Minimum time taken to burn the BT from a.pitfalls: The result counts elapsed edges, not number of layers. Target membership is validated.

Count total nodes in a complete BT.problem: Count nodes in a COMPLETE binary tree; incomplete arbitrary trees violate this shortcut's contract.
Count total nodes in a complete BT.approach: In a complete subtree, equal leftmost/rightmost heights prove it is perfect, with 2^height-1 nodes. Otherwise recurse; at least one side is perfect at each level.
Count total nodes in a complete BT.complexity: O(log² n) time; O(log n) stack on complete trees.
Count total nodes in a complete BT.trace: Sample extreme heights both three, so 2³-1=7.
Count total nodes in a complete BT.pitfalls: Equal extreme heights alone do not prove perfection for arbitrary trees; completeness is essential. Shift overflow is explicitly rejected.

Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List.problem: Flatten in place into preorder order along right links; every left becomes null.
Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List.approach: Splice each left subtree before the current right subtree, attaching old right to its rightmost boundary. This preserves root-left-right visitation.
Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List.trace: Root 4 places left subtree 2 before 6; node 2 places 1 before 3; final right chain is preorder.
Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List.pitfalls: The original shape is destroyed. Returned chain reuses existing node identities.

Requirements needed to construct a uniqu.theory: With DISTINCT labels, inorder plus preorder or inorder plus postorder uniquely determines a binary tree. Root comes from preorder first or postorder last; its inorder position divides left/right labels. Preorder plus postorder generally does not identify whether a lone child is left or right, so it is not unique without extra structural assumptions (such as full binary tree). Duplicate labels break unique index lookup and may admit multiple trees. Level order alone is also insufficient. Validate traversal lengths, labels and consistent subtree ranges; do not silently construct from mismatched inputs.

Construct a BT from Preorder and Inorder.problem: Construct using distinct labels, supplied traversal order then inorder. Reject inconsistent intervals and lengths.
Construct a BT from Preorder and Inorder.approach: Root is at the beginning of preorder or end of postorder. Look up its inorder position to determine left size and recurse on corresponding half-open ranges.
Construct a BT from Preorder and Inorder.complexity: Expected O(n) time with index map; O(n) map/output plus O(h) stack.
Construct a BT from Preorder and Inorder.trace: For inorder 1,2,3, root 2 divides leaf 1 from leaf 3.
Construct a BT from Preorder and Inorder.pitfalls: Duplicates are explicitly unsupported. Repeated linear inorder scans would cost O(n²) in a skewed case.

Construct a BT from Postorder and Inorde.problem: Construct using distinct labels, supplied traversal order then inorder. Reject inconsistent intervals and lengths.
Construct a BT from Postorder and Inorde.approach: Root is at the beginning of preorder or end of postorder. Look up its inorder position to determine left size and recurse on corresponding half-open ranges.
Construct a BT from Postorder and Inorde.complexity: Expected O(n) time with index map; O(n) map/output plus O(h) stack.
Construct a BT from Postorder and Inorde.trace: For inorder 1,2,3, root 2 divides leaf 1 from leaf 3.
Construct a BT from Postorder and Inorde.pitfalls: Duplicates are explicitly unsupported. Repeated linear inorder scans would cost O(n²) in a skewed case.

Serialize and De-serialize BT.problem: Round-trip tree shape and int values using preorder with # for each null reference.
Serialize and De-serialize BT.approach: Null markers make structure unambiguous. Decoder consumes one token for a root, then exactly its left and right encodings.
Serialize and De-serialize BT.complexity: O(n) token work/string size, O(h) stack plus O(n) output tree.
Serialize and De-serialize BT.trace: Leaf 1 encodes 1,#,#; attaching subtree encodings recovers every missing child.
Serialize and De-serialize BT.pitfalls: Inorder values alone cannot recover shape. Decoder rejects missing/extra tokens; token strings are untrusted data, never executable instructions.

Morris Inorder Traversal.problem: Traverse with O(1) auxiliary state by temporarily threading pointers; original links are restored on normal completion.
Morris Inorder Traversal.approach: For a left subtree, thread its rightmost node back to root. First encounter creates the thread and descends; second removes it. Inorder records root after the left subtree completes.
Morris Inorder Traversal.complexity: O(n) amortized time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding O(n) result.
Morris Inorder Traversal.trace: At 4, temporarily set 3.right=4; after traversing 2, remove that thread and continue to 6.
Morris Inorder Traversal.pitfalls: Do not stop early or throw while threads remain; that would corrupt the tree. Concurrent traversal is unsafe during threading.

Morris Preorder Traversal.problem: Traverse with O(1) auxiliary state by temporarily threading pointers; original links are restored on normal completion.
Morris Preorder Traversal.approach: For a left subtree, thread its rightmost node back to root. First encounter creates the thread and descends; second removes it. Preorder records root on first encounter.
Morris Preorder Traversal.complexity: O(n) amortized time, O(1) auxiliary space excluding O(n) result.
Morris Preorder Traversal.trace: At 4, temporarily set 3.right=4; after traversing 2, remove that thread and continue to 6.
Morris Preorder Traversal.pitfalls: Do not stop early or throw while threads remain; that would corrupt the tree. Concurrent traversal is unsafe during threading.

Root to Given Node Path.problem: Return root-to-target path by node identity, empty if absent.
Root to Given Node Path.approach: DFS appends current root; a successful branch retains its path, while failed branches pop before returning. Identity is unambiguous even when values repeat.
Root to Given Node Path.trace: To node5, failed left branch backtracks; right path4,6,5 succeeds.
Root to Given Node Path.pitfalls: Do not globally reset a path after a successful find; retain exactly that branch.

Enforce Children Sum Property.problem: Increase nonnegative int values only until each nonleaf equals its child-value sum. Shape is preserved; no minimum-total-increase guarantee.
Enforce Children Sum Property.approach: If children already sum above root, raise root. Otherwise raise an existing child to root so recursion can propagate the deficit. After fixing children, assign their final sum back to root; all changes are nondecreasing.
Enforce Children Sum Property.trace: Sample left root2 rises to1+3=4; right6 to5+7=12; global root becomes4+12=16.
Enforce Children Sum Property.pitfalls: Math.addExact throws if a resulting sum exceeds int; an overflow exception can occur after earlier mutations. The separate Children Sum Property lesson CHECKS without modifying values.
